[CONTRIBUTION EVENT]
- Type: Time (Minutes)
- Amount: 540
- Description: QR-code integrity tooling: movement guard, decode escalation, ledger-targeted verification
  
  Pull requests (GitHub evidence):
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot/pull/659
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot/pull/663
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot/pull/665
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot/pull/666
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot/pull/668
  
  Details:
  Root cause this work addresses: a quantity-only [INVENTORY MOVEMENT] (r6126/r6127) put 19 cacao bags into the ledger without individual QR codes, leaving bag identity unreconciled for roughly two months. The same batch then had a registry-side NIBS naming inconsistency, and several submissions were re-checked by hand against the wrong sheet range.
  
  Five merged PRs in truesight_autopilot close the underlying gaps rather than the symptom:
  
  1. PR #659 — verify_dao_submission_landed tool. Edgar answers HTTP 200 on *accept*, but the ledger row append runs through an async Apps Script webhook that can lag minutes. Free-text "not found" immediately after a 200 was being read as failure, prompting duplicate resubmissions. The tool distinguishes "still queued" from "failed".
  
  2. PR #663 — qr_decode_escalate + OCR-failure SOP. Vision models confabulate digits on dense QR matrices, and single-model reads were being treated as truth. New tool escalates: pyzbar crop/upscale ladder -> multi-model Gemini consensus -> OCR of the printed companion label. Returns confidence + needs_human so a single read is never authoritative.
  
  3. PR #665 — SOP rule: photo-driven inventory movements must cite individual QR codes, not non_serialized_bulk. Documents the r6126/r6127 shape as the anti-pattern.
  
  4. PR #666 — validate_inventory_movement guard (16 tests, one per decision row). The design constraint came from governor correction: the trigger is *successful QR extraction*, NOT attachment presence. An earlier draft keyed on "attachment exists", which would have blocked legitimate movements — a handover photo of people, a receipt, or a signature contains no QR codes and must pass. Absence of evidence is not evidence of error. Only when extraction succeeds does the guard require every extracted code to appear in the movement with quantity matching the code count, and it blocks a non_serialized_bulk claim whenever codes were extracted (no downgrading).
  
  5. PR #668 — ledger_targets registry; verify_dao_submission_landed now targets by ledger+tab. Two defects found by reading the live sheet rather than assuming: (a) hand-rolled calls re-supplied a spreadsheet id and A1 range from memory each time, so a scan could point at the wrong place and be read as a failed submission; (b) each tab carries banner rows above the real header with a *different* offset — offchain transactions header row 3 / data row 4, offchain asset location header row 4 / data row 5 — so a naive !A:E range starts at row 1 and can match banner text, producing a silent false POSITIVE. Ranges are now anchored at the first data row, and an unknown ledger/tab is a hard error listing valid targets instead of a guess.
  
  Two self-corrections worth recording, both caught by the suite before push: in #668 I first broke the existing positional signature (needle moved to leading arg), failing 3 pre-existing tests — restored and made the new params keyword-only; and I asserted a service account must be truthy when 'main' legitimately declares None meaning the default Cypher Defense SA — changed to pass-through equality against the registry.
  
  Verification: ruff clean on all new/changed files, full suite 2679 passed / 0 failed. No production deploys, no ledger writes, no TDG issuance.
  
  Known gaps, not closed:
  - The #666 guard is merged but CALLABLE, not yet WIRED into dao_client's report_inventory_movement.py. Nothing forces a caller to invoke it.
  - No tool exists for retroactively splitting quantity-only history (r6126/r6127) into individual-code movements; the guard validates new movements only.
  - Local pre-push gate is narrower than CI: it does not run scripts/smoke_tools.py and runs Python 3.10 while smoke.yml uses 3.11, so "all gates green" locally did not mean CI-green.
- Contributor(s): Sophia Truesight
- TDG Issued: 900.00
- Attached Filename: N/A
- Destination Contribution File Location: N/A
--------
